plotting_plan.objective: Bar chart showing operation detection accuracy, collection identification accuracy, and field extraction (Jaccard) for each of the 10 DetectX operations plus EdgeCase, demonstrating 100% operation detection across all types.

plotting_plan.objective: Stacked bar or waterfall chart showing S1, S2, S3, S4 latency contributions, highlighting that S1 (LLM inference) dominates at ~44s while S2 (MongoDB) is sub-10ms.

introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: IoT sensor deployments generate massive volumes of time-series data, but non-technical users cannot query this data without learning MongoDB query syntax, creating a critical accessibility gap in smart building and environmental monitoring applications.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Existing text-to-SQL and natural language interface tools (Spider, DIN-SQL, etc.) target tabular relational databases and cannot handle IoT-specific operations such as anomaly detection, trend analysis, cross-collection comparison, or time-aware aggregation — operations essential for sensor data analysis.

time-series databases and natural language interfaces for time-series data
MongoDB query generation from natural language

related_work_strategy.overview: We organize related work into three clusters: (1) text-to-SQL semantic parsing systems, (2) LLM-based query generation and code synthesis, and (3) IoT data platforms and sensor query interfaces. Each cluster reveals specific limitations that Text2Query addresses.

subsections.methodology_cluster: Semantic parsing and text-to-SQL systems that translate natural language to SQL queries
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Investigate Spider, DIN-SQL, NatSQL, and other text-to-SQL benchmarks and systems to understand their operation scope, schema handling, and evaluation methodology
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Existing text-to-SQL systems are designed for tabular relational databases and cannot express IoT-specific operations such as anomaly detection (DetectAnomaly), time-bucketed trend aggregation (DetectTrend), or cross-collection comparison (DetectCompare) within a single query language
limitation_search_queries: DIN-SQL natural language to SQL generation
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Text2Query addresses this by introducing the QueryPlan intermediate representation with 10 IoT-specific operation types that map to MongoDB aggregation pipelines, going beyond SQL's SELECT/WHERE/GROUP BY paradigm to support statistical operations native to sensor data analysis.

subsections.subsection_title: LLM-Based Query Generation and Code Synthesis
subsections.methodology_cluster: Large language models used for generating database queries, code, and structured outputs from natural language
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Investigate how LLMs (GPT, Qwen, DeepSeek) are used for query generation, code synthesis, and structured prediction tasks
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: LLM-only approaches for query generation suffer from hallucination, schema mismatch, and lack of deterministic fallback when the model produces invalid queries, leading to unreliable production deployment
limitation_search_queries: LLM code generation natural language query synthesis
Qwen large language model structured output generation
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Text2Query uses a hybrid approach: LLM-based parsing (99% success rate) with regex fallback (deterministic and 100% reliable), plus a QueryPlan intermediate representation that enables validation and self-repair before query execution, combining the flexibility of LLMs with the reliability of pattern-based parsing.

subsections.subsection_title: IoT Data Platforms and Sensor Query Interfaces
subsections.methodology_cluster: Platforms and tools for managing, querying, and visualizing IoT sensor data
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Investigate existing IoT data management platforms, time-series databases, and sensor data visualization tools that provide query interfaces
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Current IoT platforms (Grafana, InfluxDB, Kibana) require users to learn query languages or construct dashboards manually; none offer a natural language interface that handles the full pipeline from question to answer with visualization
limitation_search_queries: IoT sensor data management platform natural language
indoor air quality monitoring system data query
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Text2Query provides an end-to-end pipeline from natural language to answer with automatic visualization, specifically designed for IoT sensor data operations. It goes beyond dashboard-style monitoring by supporting statistical aggregations, anomaly detection, and cross-collection comparisons through a natural language interface.

content_bullets: Describe the four-stage pipeline architecture with data flow diagram (Fig. 1): S1 Decomposer → QueryPlan → S2 Query → Raw data → S3 Answer → S4 Visualization
Detail the QueryPlan intermediate representation: operation type (10 types), target collections, fields, time scope, and self-repair mechanism
Explain S1 Decomposer: LLM-based parsing using Qwen3.5:397B-cloud with regex fallback for robustness; self-repair mechanism that corrects malformed QueryPlans
Explain S2 Query: MongoDB query generation from QueryPlan; time-aware filtering with REFERENCE_DATE support; aggregation pipelines for statistical operations
Explain S3 Answer: LLM-based natural language answer generation from retrieved data context
Explain S4 Visualization: Context-aware Plotly chart generation for trend, compare, and anomaly queries; fallback to HTML if Kaleido unavailable

content_bullets: Open-source release on GitHub enables community adoption and extension
Direct applicability to smart building management, indoor air quality monitoring, and environmental compliance
The modular 4-stage architecture allows replacement of individual components (e.g., swapping LLM, adding new operation types, supporting different databases)
Sub-50ms S2 query latency enables real-time integration with building management systems
Text2Query is a four-stage open-source pipeline for querying IoT sensor data in natural language, achieving 100% operation detection and 96.1% collection identification on 205 benchmark questions
The hybrid LLM + regex approach with self-repair provides both flexibility and reliability
The QueryPlan intermediate representation supports 10 IoT-specific operation types beyond SQL's expressiveness
Stage-independent evaluation reveals S1 (parsing) and S2 (data retrieval) as the primary bottleneck areas for future improvement
S2 data hit rate (63.9%) is limited by time-scoped queries referencing current dates against historical data; REFERENCE_DATE mitigates this but requires user awareness
Cloud LLM latency (~44s per query) is the dominant bottleneck; local LLM deployment or caching could reduce this
Current evaluation covers three MongoDB collections in the IAQ domain; cross-domain evaluation (e.g., healthcare, industrial IoT) remains future work
User study (planned but not yet conducted) would provide qualitative validation of natural language interpretation quality
